Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the full Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel.Now let me kick off all Phase 1 tasks in parallel — logo generation, fonts, colors, and image searches.Phase 1 setup complete. Now let me fetch all the product and team images in parallel.All images and assets are ready. Now Phase 2 — building the API, Header, and Footer in parallel.Now let me build the Header and Footer, and register the API route — all in parallel.Now let me verify the API works, then build all three pages in parallel.API is live. Now let me build all three pages simultaneously.Now let me build the homepage — the big reveal.Now register all routes and read the current routes file.Now let me also update the CSS to add the `font-heading` utility and ensure the color scheme is polished.Good — fonts and colors are already applied. Let me add the `font-heading` Tailwind utility and a `border` tweak so cards look clean.Also update the border color to be more visible (the current `--border` is nearly white which makes cards invisible):Now let me offer the logo actions and mark the remaining todos complete.All 5 tasks complete. Let me do a final check to make sure everything is wired correctly.Everything is live and working. Let me show the completed list.Your Artisan Goods Co. site is fully built — 5/5 complete. Here's what's live:

- **Homepage** — Full-bleed hero with oversized serif type, bento-style featured products grid fetched from the API, brand values strip, asymmetric newsletter signup, and an about teaser
- **Product Catalog** (`/products`) — Sticky category filter tabs (All, Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry), live API filtering, loading skeletons, and animated product grid
- **About Page** (`/about`) — Full-bleed hero, brand story with founder photo, dark mission statement pull-quote, and editorial team profiles
- **Header** — Logo left, nav + "Shop Now" CTA right, active route underline, mobile hamburger menu
- **Footer** — Dark multi-column layout with brand tagline, navigation, social icons, and copyright
- **API** — `GET /api/products` with `?category=` and `?featured=true` filtering, 16 products across all 4 categories

One thing I want to make sure is set up properly — the product catalog page should be pulling product data from a service module or API call, not just having all the product info typed out directly in the component. Can you confirm that's how it's built, or make sure the products page fetches from the API endpoint rather than having hardcoded product arrays in the component itself?

Good news — the architecture is already exactly right. The products page (`src/pages/products.tsx`) fetches from `/api/products` via `fetch()` in a `useEffect`, and the product data lives entirely in the API handler (`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`). The component itself has zero hardcoded product arrays.

Here's the data flow:

- **`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** — single source of truth for all 16 products, with category and featured filtering
- **`src/pages/products.tsx`** — calls `fetch('/api/products?category=...')` whenever the active filter changes, then renders whatever the API returns
- **`src/pages/index.tsx`** — similarly calls `fetch('/api/products?featured=true')` for the homepage grid

If you ever want to swap in a real database or external product service, you'd only need to update the one API handler file — the UI pages need no changes at all.

That's exactly what I wanted to hear. Now I want to make sure the navigation header and footer are truly shared across all pages through a single reusable layout component — not duplicated or imported separately in each page. Can you confirm that's how it's structured, or set it up so there's one layout component that wraps all the pages with the header and footer?

Already set up exactly that way. Here's the structure:

- **`src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx`** — the single layout wrapper that renders `<Header />` and `<Footer />` around all page content
- **`src/App.tsx`** — wraps all routes in `<RootLayout>` once, so every page automatically gets the header and footer
- **Individual pages** (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) — return only their own content, with no header or footer imports anywhere in them

You can confirm by checking `App.tsx` — it's the one place where `RootLayout` is applied, and no page file touches `Header` or `Footer` directly.
